welcome.label: Welcome · meet Sam

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: The Red Water Sample
parts.body: What is hiding in the water at Palmetto Beach, and which tool can find it?

welcome.script:
(Hold up a clear glass of water.) This looks clean, right? But is it empty? Today we find out.

[ON SCREEN: Strange water]
This is a real Florida beach. Look at the color of the water near the shore. Something made it red-brown, and fish are washing up.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
We have a new crew member for this unit: Sam Park, an engineer who builds tools. Sam has a jar of this water. Press Listen to meet Sam, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · the beach alert and the zoom machine (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
[ON SCREEN: The beach alert]
First, play the beach alert. People noticed three things with their eyes. But could anyone see what caused them?

[ON SCREEN: The last stop]
Then use Sam’s zoom machine. Each stop is a stronger tool. Here’s a sneak peek of the last stop. What do you think this is? Press Listen for Sam’s tip.

part1.label: Part 1 · how small can each tool go? (Clue 2)
part1.script:
[ON SCREEN: Four tools]
Scientists start simple. If your eyes can do the job, you don’t need a microscope. Sort each card onto the weakest tool that shows it clearly. Press Listen.

part3.label: Part 3 · pick the right tool (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🧪 Four lab requests
parts.title: Which tool fits the question?
parts.body: Count living cells? See one cell’s surface? Look at a wing at a picnic?

parts.label: ⚡ The catch
parts.title: The strongest tool can’t do every job
parts.body: An electron microscope needs a dried sample. Nothing on it can be alive.

part3.script:
(Hold up something big, like a backpack, and pretend to look at it through a tiny tube.) Is the strongest tool always the best? Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: Four lab requests]
Sam’s lab got four requests. Read each one and think: what does the question ask you to DO?

[ON SCREEN: The catch]
Here’s the catch: the electron microscope sees the most, but it can’t look at anything alive. Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · count the cells (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🔬 Sam’s microscope
parts.title: Slide, lens, focus, count
rows: Count the cells in the square

parts.label: 📋 The lab report
parts.title: Match the real FWC chart
parts.body: Florida scientists use this chart to warn people at the beach.

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: Sam’s microscope]
Time to use a real scientist’s routine. Slide on, strongest lens, then turn the focus knob slowly. Watch the cells get sharp. Count only the ones inside the square.

[ON SCREEN: The lab report]
Then fill in Sam’s lab report and find your number on the real chart. How bad is the red tide? Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What is in the water?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to write
rows: Three views of one small thing
Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, three views of one small thing for Part C, and your CER. Pick something you can really find, like a leaf or a grain of sand. Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “You should always use the most powerful tool you can find. The more magnification, the better.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says the most powerful tool is always best. Would you bring an electron microscope to a picnic to look at a bee? Could it count living red tide cells?

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🧫 Your specimen
parts.title: Red tide sample slide
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Tools for things far away
parts.body: Telescopes: how do we see the Moon and the planets up close?

closing.script:
Case closed! You found red tide hiding in the water, and you picked the right tool for every job.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and Sam’s red tide slide goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time we flip it around: tools for things that are really far away. Press Listen for Sam’s last word.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
